```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ggrepel)
library(kableExtra)

dat <- readRDS("../../output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds")

# one row per study: metadata are shared by the increased and decreased signatures
studies <- dat |>
  distinct(Study, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, -`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, -`Abundance in Group 1`) |>
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

# colors: health/periodontitis, periodontitis classification, profiling method
# (method colors match the overview figure of the main report; grey is always "not reported")
pal_group <- c(Health = "#2a78d6", Periodontitis = "#eb6834")

class_levels <- c(
  "Chronic periodontitis", "Chronic and aggressive periodontitis", "Aggressive periodontitis",
  "Periodontitis (stage/grade)", "Refractory periodontitis", "Periodontitis (type not specified)"
)
class_short <- c("Chronic", "Chronic + aggressive", "Aggressive", "Stage/grade", "Refractory", "Not specified")
pal_class <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6", "#e87ba4", "#eda100", "#e34948", "grey65"), class_short)

method_levels <- c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics", "DNA-DNA hybridization",
                   "PCR", "Other / not reported")
pal_method <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#008300", "#d55181", "grey65"), method_levels)

theme_meta <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
theme_set(theme_meta)

studies <- studies |>
  mutate(
    classification = factor(
      class_short[match(`Periodontitis classification`, class_levels)], levels = class_short
    ),
    method = case_when(
      `Sequencing type` == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
      `Sequencing type` == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
      `Sequencing type` %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
      `Sequencing platform` == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
      .default = "Other / not reported"
    ) |> factor(levels = method_levels),
    period = cut(Year, c(-Inf, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, Inf),
                 labels = c("1995–2004", "2005–2009", "2010–2014", "2015–2019", "2020–2025"))
  )

# group-level measures in long format
features <- tribble(
  ~feature,   ~label,                          ~mean_col,                        ~sd_col,
  "age",      "Age (years)",                   "age mean",                       "age sd",
  "males",    "Males (%)",                     "percent males",                  NA,
  "smokers",  "Smokers (%)",                   "percent smokers",                NA,
  "pd",       "Probing depth (mm)",            "pocket depth mean (mm)",         "pocket depth sd",
  "cal",      "Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "clinical attachment loss (mm)",  "clinical attachment loss sd",
  "bop",      "Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "bleeding on probing percent",    "bleeding on probing sd",
  "plaque",   "Plaque (% sites)",              "plaque",                         "plaque sd",
  "supp",     "Suppuration (% sites)",         "suppuration percent",            "suppuration sd"
) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label))

long <- pmap_dfr(features, function(feature, label, mean_col, sd_col) {
  map_dfr(0:1, function(g) {
    col <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) NA_real_ else studies[[paste("Group", g, x)]]
    num <- if (feature %in% c("males", "smokers")) col(paste("num", feature)) else NA_real_
    tibble(
      Study = studies$Study, feature = feature, label = label,
      group = c("Health", "Periodontitis")[g + 1],
      mean = col(mean_col), sd = col(sd_col),
      n = studies[[paste("Group", g, "sample size")]],
      num = num
    )
  })
}) |>
  # plaque indices (e.g. Silness-Löe 0-3) are not comparable with % sites
  left_join(select(studies, Study, `Plaque measure`), by = "Study") |>
  filter(!is.na(mean), feature != "plaque" | `Plaque measure` %in% "% sites") |>
  select(-`Plaque measure`)

# studies with values for both groups
paired <- long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Study, feature, label), names_from = group,
              values_from = c(mean, sd, n, num)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_Health), !is.na(mean_Periodontitis)) |>
  # smokers excluded from both groups: no contrast
  filter(!(feature == "smokers" & mean_Health == 0 & mean_Periodontitis == 0))

paired_tests <- paired |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    diff = median(mean_Periodontitis - mean_Health),
    p = wilcox.test(mean_Periodontitis, mean_Health, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = c(feature, label)
  ) |>
  mutate(p_label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste("p =", signif(p, 2))))
```

## About this report

This report describes PerioSigDB: how participant and clinical characteristics differ between periodontitis and comparison groups and across studies, how PerioSigDB compares with BugSigDB, and how the taxa it links to periodontitis are reported in other conditions.

The metadata summaries use the **study** as the unit of analysis (n = `r nrow(studies)`), because metadata are recorded once per study and shared by its increased and decreased signatures. Later comparisons use studies, study units or signatures, as stated for each figure.

Group 1 is the periodontitis group and Group 0 the comparison group. The comparison group is labelled "Health" in the figures, but eligibility criteria varied:

- Studies 298, 153 and 155 include participants with gingivitis in Group 0.
- Studies 1752, 1818 and 1897 recruited adults aged 65 and over described as periodontitis-resistant.

::: {.callout-note}
## Terms used in this report

- **Study:** an individual published research study.
- **Signature:** a list of taxa reported as increased or decreased in one group compared with another. "Increased" and "decreased" are reported case–control differences, not changes over time.
- **Study unit:** a unique combination of study, condition, direction and body site group (BugSigDB analyses), so that a study with several similar signatures counts once.
- **Enrichment (literature analyses):** a genus is reported in a given direction by a larger share of a condition's studies than expected from other studies. It describes how often the genus is reported, not how much more abundant it is in participants.
- **Periodontitis-increased / -decreased genera:** the genera most consistently reported increased or decreased in PerioSigDB. Several health-associated oral taxa are in the decreased group, but a genus can contain species reported in both directions (e.g. *Porphyromonas gingivalis* increased, *P. catoniae* decreased).
- **FDR < 0.05:** p-values adjusted for the number of tests with the Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) method, at a false discovery rate of 5%. "Unadjusted p" is the p-value before this adjustment.
:::

The analyses use several sets of periodontitis taxa:

| Taxon set | Selection rule | Rank | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top 20 genera per direction | the 20 genera per direction with the smallest binomial p-value (increased vs decreased PerioSigDB signatures); includes genera that do not pass FDR | genus | genus heatmaps, direction summary, prevalence, co-occurrence |
| Consensus signatures (33 increased, 13 decreased taxa) | binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, p < 0.05 | as reported (mostly species) | whole-signature similarity, taxon-by-taxon heatmaps |
| Genus consensus (17 and 8 genera) | the consensus signatures collapsed to genus | genus | Jaccard overlap, participant-level colorectal cancer analysis |
| Descriptive taxon sets (head and neck cancer, smoking) | reported by at least 3 studies, at least 75% in one direction; no statistical test | as reported | taxon-by-taxon heatmaps |

**Assay coverage:** about half of PerioSigDB signatures come from targeted PCR or DNA–DNA hybridization, which measure a predefined list of taxa. Reporting frequencies in this report therefore reflect both biological findings and which taxa the original assays could detect or were designed to measure. A signature does not distinguish a taxon that was measured and unchanged, measured but not reported, or not measured, so absence from a signature is not evidence that a taxon was absent or unchanged.

# Data availability

## Metadata completeness heatmap

```{r completeness}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Reporting of metadata across studies. Each column is a study, ordered by publication year (ticks: first study of each period); each row is a field. Group-level fields are shaded by whether they are reported for both groups, one group, or neither. Plaque counts as reported only when given as % of sites. Systemic health status is shaded when recorded, whether systemically healthy or not; systemic comorbidity is shaded only when participants are recorded as having a systemic condition (e.g. diabetes), so it is not a completeness measure. The percentage after each field is the share of studies reporting it for both groups (group-level fields) or at all (study-level fields)."

study_fields <- tibble(
  Study = studies$Study,
  `Profiling method` = studies$method != "Other / not reported",
  `16S variable region` = !is.na(studies$`16S variable region`),
  `Periodontitis classification` = studies$classification != "Not specified",
  `Systemic health status` = !is.na(studies$`Systemic condition`),
  `Systemic comorbidity recorded as present` = !is.na(studies$`Systemic condition`) &
    studies$`Systemic condition` != "systemically healthy",
  `Group 0 definition` = !is.na(studies$`Group 0 definition`),
  `Group 1 definition` = !is.na(studies$`Group 1 definition`)
) |>
  pivot_longer(-Study, names_to = "field", values_to = "reported") |>
  mutate(status = ifelse(reported, "Reported", "Not reported"), type = "Study")

size_fields <- studies |>
  transmute(Study, n0 = !is.na(`Group 0 sample size`), n1 = !is.na(`Group 1 sample size`)) |>
  mutate(field = "Sample size")

group_fields <- long |>
  distinct(Study, label, group) |>
  count(Study, field = as.character(label), name = "groups") |>
  complete(Study = studies$Study, field = levels(features$label), fill = list(groups = 0)) |>
  bind_rows(transmute(size_fields, Study, field, groups = n0 + n1)) |>
  mutate(
    status = c("Neither group", "One group", "Both groups")[groups + 1],
    type = "Group"
  )

completeness <- bind_rows(group_fields, study_fields) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(
    Study = fct_reorder(Study, Year, .fun = min),
    complete = status %in% c("Both groups", "Reported")
  ) |>
  mutate(field_label = paste0(field, " (", round(100 * mean(complete)), "%)"), .by = field)

field_order <- completeness |>
  summarise(pct = mean(complete), type = first(type), .by = field_label) |>
  arrange(type == "Study", pct) |>
  pull(field_label)

pal_status <- c(
  "Both groups" = "#2a78d6", "One group" = "#9ec5f4", "Neither group" = "#f0efec",
  "Reported" = "#256abf", "Not reported" = "#f0efec"
)

# year ticks: first study of each publication period
year_ticks <- studies |>
  arrange(Year) |>
  distinct(period, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(Study, Year)

ggplot(completeness, aes(x = Study, y = factor(field_label, levels = field_order), fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_status, breaks = c("Both groups", "One group", "Neither group")) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = year_ticks$Study, labels = year_ticks$Year) +
  labs(x = "Studies (ordered by publication year)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank())
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each cell:** one study (column) × one field (row); all 128 studies. Columns ordered by publication year (1995–2025; ties in alphabetical order of study ID). Axis ticks label the first study of each period: 1995, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020.
- **Rows:** group-level fields (bottom block, sorted by completeness, lowest at bottom) then study-level fields (top block, same sorting). The % in each label is the share of the 128 studies that are dark blue in that row.
- **Group-level fields:** come from the `Group 0 …` and `Group 1 …` columns of the PerioSigDB sheet (`age mean`, `percent males`, `percent smokers`, `pocket depth mean (mm)`, `clinical attachment loss (mm)`, `bleeding on probing percent`, `plaque`, `suppuration percent`, `sample size`). A group counts as reported if its mean/percentage is non-missing; SDs are not considered. Group 0 is the comparison group, Group 1 periodontitis.
- **Plaque:** counted only when `Plaque measure` is "% sites" (41 studies have that measure); the 16 studies reporting a plaque index (e.g. Silness–Löe) count as "Neither group" even though a value is in the sheet.
- **Study-level fields:** profiling method is reported unless it falls in "Other / not reported" (method derived from `Sequencing type`: 16S, WMS → shotgun, PCR or 16S,PCR → PCR; otherwise `Sequencing platform` = DNA-DNA Hybridization; else other/not reported). Classification counts as reported unless "Periodontitis (type not specified)" (46 studies). Group definitions count as reported if non-empty, so the literal entry "ND" (10 Group 0, 2 Group 1 definitions) counts as reported.
- **Systemic rows:** `Systemic condition` non-missing → status shaded (67 studies: 55 "systemically healthy", 12 with a named condition); comorbidity row shaded only for those 12.
- **"One group" cells:** mostly missing comparison-group values for clinical measures (e.g. BOP: 10 studies with only the periodontitis group, 4 with only the comparison group); smokers lean the other way (6 comparison-only, 2 periodontitis-only). Sample size: Study 2264 lacks the Group 1 size; Studies 887 and 1590 lack both.
- **Example:** age is reported for both groups in 106 studies (83%), for one group in 4 (Studies 448, 1988, 2067, 2095), neither in 18.
- **Watch out:** study-level "Reported" uses a slightly darker blue than "Both groups" and is not in the legend. 16S variable region is a % of all 128 studies (18), not of 16S studies (18 of the 34 studies with sequencing type 16S or 16S,PCR).
:::

**Shows:** availability varies substantially across metadata fields, particularly for systemic health status and several clinical measures. Changes over time in the classification used are shown in "Periodontitis classification over time and by method".

**Caveat:** "Not reported" can also mean "not entered". Systemic health status was not extracted for about half the studies in the original overview sheet, so studies with comorbid participants may be missed.

# Health vs periodontitis

## Paired study-level comparison

```{r paired-slopes}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Health (comparison group) vs periodontitis within each study. Small points: the group mean reported by each study; grey lines join the two groups of one study; large points: median of the group means across studies, for each group separately. n: studies reporting the measure for both groups; median difference: median across studies of the periodontitis minus health difference (not the difference between the two large points); p: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across studies."

medians <- long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  summarise(median = median(mean), .by = c(label, group))

strip_labels <- paired_tests |>
  arrange(label) |>
  mutate(strip = paste0(label, "\nn = ", studies, ", median difference ", sprintf("%+.2g", diff), "\n", p_label)) |>
  mutate(strip = factor(strip, levels = strip)) |>
  select(label, strip)

long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  left_join(strip_labels, by = "label") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = mean)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Study), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = group), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
            aes(y = median, group = 1), color = "grey15", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
             aes(y = median, fill = group), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 4, stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~strip, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_group, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_group) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Data:** studies with a non-missing Group 0 and Group 1 value for the measure (same columns as in the completeness heatmap; plaque only when measured as % sites). Smokers: 43 studies with 0% in both groups (smokers excluded by design) are dropped, leaving 38 of 81. No other exclusions; e.g. Study 136 (all female) stays in males at 0% → 0%.
- **Small points/lines:** one study's reported group mean (or percentage); x position Health = Group 0 (comparison group), Periodontitis = Group 1. Free y axis per panel.
- **Large points:** median across the same studies of each group's values separately: age 37.4 vs 44.8 y; males 39.5 vs 41.1%; smokers 10.4 vs 28.5%; PD 2.0 vs 3.9 mm; CAL 1.23 vs 3.9 mm; BOP 6.0 vs 54.4%; plaque 20.6 vs 61.2%; suppuration 0 vs 2.5%.
- **Strip numbers:** n = studies with both groups; median difference = median of per-study (periodontitis − comparison) differences, printed to 2 significant figures (age +4.8, males +2.3, smokers +14, PD +2, CAL +2.5, BOP +45, plaque +39, suppuration +2.5).
- **Test:** paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test of Group 1 vs Group 0 values, two-sided, unit = study, normal approximation with continuity correction (`exact = FALSE`); zero differences are dropped. Unadjusted across the 8 measures; all are p < 0.001 except males (p = 0.016).
- **Direction counts (not shown):** periodontitis group higher in every study for PD (81/81), CAL (62), BOP (51), plaque (34), suppuration (18); age 85 higher, 20 lower, 1 tie; males 57 / 35 / 8 ties; smokers 34 / 3 / 1.
- **Example:** Study 147 (2005, chronic periodontitis) reports age 37.5 → 47.2 y, males 53.3% → 38.5%, smokers 0% → 7.7%, PD 1.5 → 3.7 mm; it contributes one line to each of those four panels.
- **Watch out:** each study counts equally regardless of sample size; group values are study-reported means, so PD/CAL may be full-mouth or sampled-site values.
:::

**Shows:** the size and consistency of the health–periodontitis difference for each measure, and how much individual studies vary around it. Within most studies, the periodontitis group had higher reported values for the clinical measures. The demographic measures show imbalances between groups: periodontitis groups were generally older and included a higher proportion of smokers.

**Caveat:** each study counts equally, regardless of its sample size.

## Participant characteristics and clinical measures by periodontitis classification

```{r within-perio}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values across studies, by the periodontitis classification reported (one point per study). Bars are medians; numbers below are the studies in each panel. Smokers at 0% are mostly studies that excluded smokers."

within <- long |>
  filter(group == "Periodontitis", feature %in% c("age", "smokers", "pd", "cal", "bop")) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, classification), by = "Study")

ggplot(within, aes(x = classification, y = mean, color = classification)) +
  geom_quasirandom(size = 1.8, width = 0.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey15") +
  geom_text(data = count(within, label, classification), aes(y = -Inf, label = n), vjust = -0.5,
            size = 2.8, color = "grey35") +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_class) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** one study's periodontitis-group (Group 1) mean or percentage; only Group 1 is used, so studies missing the comparison-group value are included (unlike the paired figure).
- **Data:** age, smokers, PD, CAL and BOP only (males, plaque, suppuration not shown). Smokers include 0% values (43 of 83 studies), i.e. no exclusion of smoker-free studies.
- **Classification:** from the `Periodontitis classification` column, shortened: Chronic, Chronic + aggressive (studies including both), Aggressive, Stage/grade (2017/2018 classification), Refractory, Not specified ("type not specified").
- **Bars:** median per classification. Medians (age / smokers / PD / CAL / BOP): Chronic 46.4 / 0 / 4.0 / 4.2 / 54.4; Chronic + aggressive 40.4 / 28.8 / 4.57 / 4.12 / 59.4; Aggressive 26.8 / 0 / 4.43 / 4.41 / 72; Stage/grade 45.6 / 0 / 3.59 / 3.86 / 65.5; Not specified 46 / 20 / 4.1 / 3.1 / 49.
- **Numbers below:** studies per box. Age: 38, 10, 8, 15, 1, 35 (Chronic → Not specified order); smokers 31, 7, 5, 14, 1, 25; PD 33, 8, 8, 14, 1, 26; CAL 26, 6, 7, 12, 1, 19; BOP 25, 5, 5, 10, 1, 15.
- **Example:** Refractory is one study (Study 1867): age 51, smokers 59%, PD 3.9 mm, CAL 4.2 mm, BOP 53%, so its "bar" is that single value. Aggressive age values range from 23.7 (Study 1085) to 39.4 (Study 1986).
- **No test:** descriptive only.
- **Watch out:** a smokers median of 0 (Chronic, Aggressive, Stage/grade) reflects studies that excluded smokers, not low smoking among recruited patients.
:::

**Shows:** whether "periodontitis" means comparable disease across studies. Studies using the historical aggressive-periodontitis classification generally included younger participants, and their reported probing depths tended to be higher than in some other categories, although the distributions overlap substantially. Unspecified and stage/grade studies span a wide range.

**Caveat:** some categories have few studies (e.g. refractory n = 1). Some studies report PD and CAL for the sampled sites rather than the full mouth. These values are not directly comparable and may be higher when sampling targets deeper or more affected sites.

## Participant characteristics of studies reporting the top consensus taxa

```{r consensus-taxa-characteristics}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group probing depth, age and share of males in the studies reporting each of the top 10 consensus taxa in its consensus direction (rows; red: increased, blue: decreased in periodontitis; ordered by the number of PerioSigDB signatures reporting the taxon in that direction, most at top). One point per study; boxes: median and interquartile range; whiskers: up to 1.5 × the interquartile range. Grey: all PerioSigDB studies with a value, for reference. Numbers at right: studies in each box. Consensus taxa: binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, unadjusted p < 0.05."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R
consensus_tests <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")[c("consensus", "taxon_tests")]

# each signature's taxa as terminal NCBI IDs with their names
sig_taxa <- tibble(
  Study = dat$Study, direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  id = map(dat$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, \(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", sub("^.*[|]", "", x))),
  name = map(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, \(x) sub("^.*[|][a-z]__", "", x))
) |>
  unnest(c(id, name))

top_consensus <- tibble(
  id = unlist(consensus_tests$consensus),
  direction = rep(names(consensus_tests$consensus), lengths(consensus_tests$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(select(consensus_tests$taxon_tests, id = ids, increased, decreased), by = "id") |>
  mutate(n_sigs = ifelse(direction == "increased", increased, decreased)) |>
  slice_max(n_sigs, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE, by = direction) |>
  left_join(distinct(sig_taxa, id, name), by = "id")

all_label <- "All PerioSigDB studies"
taxon_values <- filter(long, group == "Periodontitis", feature %in% c("pd", "age", "males")) |>
  select(Study, label, mean)

taxon_characteristics <- bind_rows(
  sig_taxa |>
    semi_join(top_consensus, by = c("id", "direction")) |>
    distinct(Study, direction, name) |>
    inner_join(taxon_values, by = "Study", relationship = "many-to-many"),
  map_dfr(c("increased", "decreased"), \(dir) mutate(taxon_values, direction = dir, name = all_label))
) |>
  mutate(
    name = factor(name, levels = c(all_label, rev(top_consensus$name))),
    direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                       labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")),
    label = factor(label, levels = c("Probing depth (mm)", "Age (years)", "Males (%)")),
    fill = case_when(name == all_label ~ "grey85", direction == "Increased in periodontitis" ~ "#e8a598",
                     .default = "#9fbbe0")
  )

ggplot(taxon_characteristics, aes(mean, name)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = fill), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_quasirandom(orientation = "y", size = 0.7, alpha = 0.5, width = 0.2) +
  geom_text(data = count(taxon_characteristics, direction, label, name), aes(x = Inf, label = n),
            hjust = 1.3, size = 2.6, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.12))) +
  facet_grid(direction ~ label, scales = "free", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Taxa:** from the precomputed `../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds` (`$consensus`, `$taxon_tests`; made by `scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R`). Taxa are matched by terminal NCBI ID at the reported rank (species and genus entries are separate). Per taxon: exact binomial test (`binom.test`, two-sided, p = 0.5) of PerioSigDB signatures listing it increased vs decreased; consensus = p < 0.05, unadjusted, in the majority direction (33 increased, 13 decreased taxa).
- **Rows:** the 10 consensus taxa per direction with the most signatures in their consensus direction (no ties at the cut-off). Increased: *P. gingivalis* 78, *T. forsythia* 70, *T. denticola* 46, *P. intermedia* 40, *F. alocis* 31, *C. rectus* 26, *P. endodontalis* 23, *P. micra* 22, *F. nucleatum* 21, *[Eubacterium] saphenum* 19. Decreased: *S. sanguinis* 23, *R. dentocariosa* 16, *A. naeslundii* 15, *H. parainfluenzae* 14, *C. matruchotii* 12, *L. mirabilis* 11, *R. aeria* 9, *G. adiacens* 9, *G. haemolysans* 7, *C. durum* 7.
- **Signatures = studies here:** each study has at most one increased and one decreased signature, so these counts are also study counts.
- **Each point:** one study listing the taxon in the consensus direction, placed at its periodontitis-group (Group 1) value: `pocket depth mean (mm)`, `age mean`, `percent males`. Studies missing the value are dropped from that panel, so box n is below the signature count.
- **Grey reference row:** all PerioSigDB studies with a Group 1 value (PD 90, age 107, males 104), median PD 3.98 mm, age 44.9 y, males 41.4%. The same row is repeated in both direction panels.
- **Boxes:** median and IQR; whiskers to 1.5 × IQR; outliers not drawn separately (all studies shown as points). Numbers at right: studies in the box.
- **Example:** *P. gingivalis* (78 increased, 0 decreased signatures; p = 6.6e-24): 55 of its 78 studies report Group 1 PD, median 3.96 mm (IQR 3.44–5.72) vs 3.98 mm overall. *C. matruchotii* decreased: 7 studies with PD, median 6.8 mm; *R. aeria*: 5 studies, median 6.47 mm.
- **No test:** descriptive; the same study appears in many rows (e.g. 64 of the 78 *P. gingivalis* studies also list *T. forsythia*).
:::

**Shows:** for most of the top consensus taxa, the studies reporting them have periodontitis groups with probing depths, ages and shares of males similar to PerioSigDB as a whole, so these taxa are not reported only by studies of unusually severe disease or of particular age or sex groups. The exceptions are among the less-reported decreased taxa: the few studies reporting *Corynebacterium matruchotii* and *Rothia aeria* decreased have higher median probing depths than PerioSigDB overall.

**Caveat:** this is descriptive, with no test: the same studies appear in many rows, and rows with fewer than about 10 studies are uncertain. Probing depth is reported by fewer studies than age, and some studies report it for the sampled sites rather than the full mouth, which may raise values in studies that sampled the deepest pockets.

## Trends over publication year

```{r trends}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values by publication year (one point per study). Black lines are descriptive linear fits with 95% confidence bands; each study counts equally."

within |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = mean)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "grey60", color = "white", size = 2.4, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "grey10", fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Publication year", y = NULL)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** one study's periodontitis-group (Group 1) value against its `Year`; the same studies and values as the "by periodontitis classification" figure above (age 107, smokers 83, PD 90, CAL 71, BOP 61 studies).
- **Lines:** ordinary least-squares fit of value on year per panel (`geom_smooth(method = "lm")`), unweighted, with 95% confidence band for the fitted mean.
- **Slopes (not shown, unadjusted p from the same fits):** age +2.5 y per decade (p = 0.067); smokers −7.3 percentage points per decade (p = 0.029); PD −0.05 mm (p = 0.82); CAL +0.3 mm (p = 0.21); BOP +4.3 points (p = 0.18).
- **Example:** the earliest age point is Study 155 (1995, 42.8 y); the latest BOP points include Studies 2025-PubMed-357 (70%) and 2025-224 (63.1%).
- **Watch out:** smokers include 0% from studies that excluded smokers, which drives much of that panel (and many recent stage/grade studies are at 0%). Publication year, not recruitment year.
:::

**Shows:** little change with publication year. More recent studies report somewhat older periodontitis groups (about 2.5 years per decade) and higher bleeding on probing (about 4 points per decade), but neither slope reaches p < 0.05 (p = 0.07 and 0.18, unadjusted). The share of smokers falls (about 7 points per decade, p = 0.03), partly because more recent studies often excluded smokers. These are study-level associations with publication year (not recruitment year) and may reflect changes in recruitment, case definitions, measurement or reporting. They are relevant to whether older and newer signatures are comparable.

# Study characteristics

## Periodontitis classification over time and by method

```{r classification}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Periodontitis classification of studies by publication period (share of studies; counts in bars). (B) Number of studies by classification and profiling method."

pA <- studies |>
  count(period, classification) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), .by = period) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prop, y = fct_rev(period), fill = classification)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop > 0.06, n, "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            color = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL, tag = "A") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

pB <- studies |>
  count(classification, method) |>
  complete(classification, method, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = fct_rev(classification), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, ""), color = n > 12), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = "#1c5cab", guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey15", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Data:** all 128 studies, one each; classification from `Periodontitis classification` (shortened labels; "Not specified" = type not specified), period from `Year` (1995–2004, 2005–09, 2010–14, 2015–19, 2020–25).
- **A, each bar:** one period, studies = 100%; segments are classifications. Studies per period: 14, 28, 31, 23, 32.
- **A, numbers:** study counts, printed only for segments > 6% of the bar. Hidden: 2005–09 Chronic + aggressive (1) and Refractory (1); 2015–19 Aggressive (1).
- **A, counts by period (Chronic / Chronic + aggressive / Aggressive / Stage/grade / Refractory / Not specified):** 1995–2004 1/1/2/0/0/10; 2005–09 16/1/3/0/1/7; 2010–14 10/4/3/0/0/14; 2015–19 16/3/1/0/0/3; 2020–25 3/2/0/15/0/12.
- **B, each cell:** studies with that classification and profiling method; blank = 0; white text when > 12. Method from `Sequencing type` (16S; WMS → shotgun; PCR or 16S,PCR → PCR), else `Sequencing platform` = DNA-DNA Hybridization; otherwise "Other / not reported" (18 studies with no sequencing type and a platform other than hybridization or none).
- **Example:** stage/grade studies are mostly 16S (11 of 15; 2 shotgun, 2 PCR, none hybridization); chronic studies are mostly PCR (22 of 46) and hybridization (10).
- **No test.**
:::

**Shows:** the terminology used to classify periodontitis changed over time, from the chronic/aggressive categories of the 1999 classification to staging and grading (2017 World Workshop classification, published in 2018) in the most recent period. Studies are grouped by the classification terminology they report; stage/grade is a framework rather than a disease type directly interchangeable with chronic or aggressive periodontitis. Panel B shows which classifications each profiling method has studied.

**Caveat:** "Not specified" is large. Many older studies define periodontitis only by PD/CAL thresholds.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each bar:** studies (of 128) with that `Systemic condition` entry, text as entered (sentence case), so combined entries are their own bar. Number at the end of each bar is the count.
- **Colours:** grey = missing (61 studies); blue = "systemically healthy" (55); orange = any named condition (12 studies across 8 bars).
- **Conditions:** rheumatoid arthritis 3 (Studies 129, 450, 2025-PubMed-130); COPD 2 (515, 2025-180); type 2 diabetes 2 (734, 2025-Embase-55); diabetes mellitus 1 (1411); dyspepsia 1 (126); hypertension 1 (2025-231); hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, diabetes 1 (2025-187); cardiovascular disease, diabetes (periodontitis group only) 1 (766).

**Shows:** the studies with recorded systemic comorbidities (e.g. rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension), which may warrant separate consideration in sensitivity analyses.
