# Comparison with BugSigDB

```{r bugsigdb-load}
# BugSigDB export (cached by bugsigdbr; version date from its message or warning)
bsdb_version <- NA_character_
version_from <- function(cnd) {
  if (grepl("version from", conditionMessage(cnd))) bsdb_version <<- substr(trimws(sub(".*from ", "", conditionMessage(cnd))), 1, 10)
}
bsdb <- withCallingHandlers(
  bugsigdbr::importBugSigDB(),
  message = \(m) { version_from(m); invokeRestart("muffleMessage") },
  warning = \(w) { version_from(w); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }
)
if (is.na(bsdb_version)) bsdb_version <- format(Sys.Date())

# body site group of each listed body site: the first matching pattern wins (so skin of the cheek is skin,
# the oropharynx upper airway); sites matching none are "other" (e.g. blood, milk, pancreas)
site_rules <- c(
  skin = "^skin|^cheek$|forehead|axilla|interdigital",
  eye = "conjunctiv|tear film|eyelid|meibum|ocular",
  oral = "plaque|saliva|mouth|oral cavity|oral opening|tongue|gingiv|buccal|lip$|cheek pouch",
  `upper airway` = "pharyn|throat|nasal|nose|upper respiratory|tonsil",
  `lower airway` = "lung|sputum|bronch|trachea",
  gastrointestinal = paste0("feces|colon|colorect|intestin|caecum|cecum|rectum|rectal|ileum|ileal|jejunum|duoden|",
                            "stomach|gastric|esophag|meconium|digestive|bile"),
  urogenital = "vagin|cervi|uter|endometri|ovary|fallopian|placenta|urine|urinary|urethra|genitalia|prostate|penis"
)
site_of <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  group <- rep("other", length(x))
  for (g in rev(names(site_rules))) group[grepl(site_rules[[g]], x, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- g
  group
}
# any of a signature's body sites is oral
is_oral <- function(sites) map_lgl(strsplit(sites, ","), \(x) any(site_of(x) == "oral"))

# BugSigDB without its periodontitis signatures (PerioSigDB is the reference for those)
bsdb_other <- filter(bsdb, !grepl("periodont", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE))

db_levels <- c("PerioSigDB", "BugSigDB")
pal_db <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6"), db_levels)

# genera of the taxa in a signature (taxa above genus rank are dropped)
genera <- function(x) unique(sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", x[grepl("g__", x)]))

sig_genera <- function(d) {
  tibble(
    sig = seq_len(nrow(d)), Condition = d$Condition, `Body site` = d$`Body site`,
    direction = d$`Abundance in Group 1`, taxon = map(d$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, genera)
  ) |>
    unnest(taxon)
}
```

PerioSigDB uses BugSigDB's format, so its signatures can be compared with signatures from other microbiome studies. These analyses use the BugSigDB export of `r bsdb_version`, with `r n_distinct(bsdb$PMID)` studies and `r nrow(bsdb)` signatures across all conditions and body sites. BugSigDB's own periodontitis signatures (`r nrow(bsdb) - nrow(bsdb_other)`) are excluded throughout.

## Profiling methods and taxonomic resolution

```{r bsdb-methods}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-cap: "(A) Profiling method of signatures (share of signatures). (B) Taxonomic rank of the taxa in signatures (share of taxon occurrences: a taxon listed in several signatures counts once per signature). BugSigDB includes all conditions and body sites except periodontitis."

method_of <- function(type, platform) {
  case_when(
    type == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
    type == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
    type %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
    platform == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
    .default = "Other / not reported"
  ) |>
    factor(levels = method_levels)
}

methods_db <- bind_rows(
  dat |> transmute(db = "PerioSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`)),
  bsdb_other |> transmute(db = "BugSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`))
) |>
  count(db, method) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

rank_names <- c(s = "Species", g = "Genus", f = "Family", o = "Order", c = "Class", p = "Phylum", k = "Kingdom")
pal_rank <- c(Species = "#184f95", Genus = "#3987e5", Family = "#86b6ef", Higher = "#cde2fb")

ranks_db <- bind_rows(
  tibble(db = "PerioSigDB", taxon = unlist(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`)),
  tibble(db = "BugSigDB", taxon = unlist(bsdb_other$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`))
) |>
  mutate(
    rank = rank_names[substr(sub(".*[|]", "", taxon), 1, 1)],
    rank = factor(ifelse(rank %in% c("Species", "Genus", "Family"), rank, "Higher"), levels = names(pal_rank))
  ) |>
  count(db, rank) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

stack_bar <- function(d, fill, pal, tag) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = prop, y = db, fill = {{ fill }})) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.06, scales::percent(prop, 1), "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = tag) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}

stack_bar(methods_db, method, pal_method, "A") +
  stack_bar(ranks_db, rank, pal_rank, "B") +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Unit:** signatures, not studies. PerioSigDB: all 201 signatures (125 increased, 76 decreased; 73 studies contribute two). BugSigDB: 8,114 signatures from 1,371 studies, i.e. the cached bugsigdbr export minus the 49 signatures whose `Condition` contains "periodont"; all conditions, body sites, comparisons and directions.
- **A:** method per signature, derived from `Sequencing type` and `Sequencing platform` exactly as for PerioSigDB studies. PerioSigDB: 16S 29% (58), shotgun 9.5% (19), DNA-DNA hybridization 25% (50), PCR 25% (50; includes 8 signatures typed 16S,PCR), other/not reported 12% (24). BugSigDB: 16S 83% (6,715), shotgun 15% (1,196), PCR 1% (84), hybridization 2 signatures, other 1.4% (117; 18S 9, ITS 37, no type 71).
- **B:** rank of each taxon occurrence, from the last level prefix of its MetaPhlAn name (`s__`, `g__`, `f__`; order, class, phylum, kingdom pooled as "Higher"). PerioSigDB: species 89% (1,872), genus 8% (168), family 1.2%, higher 1.4%. BugSigDB: species 32% (20,813), genus 42% (27,494), family 13%, higher 13%.
- **Bar labels:** percentages shown only for segments ≥ 6%.
- **Example:** a *P. gingivalis* entry in 78 PerioSigDB signatures adds 78 species occurrences to B.
- **No test.**
:::

**Shows:** targeted PCR and checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization together account for about half of PerioSigDB signatures, and most reported taxa are species. BugSigDB signatures come predominantly from sequencing studies and include a broader mix of taxonomic ranks, with genus the largest category. This is the main structural difference between the two databases, and it is why the comparison of taxa across conditions below works at genus level.

**Caveat:** targeted assays measure a predefined list of taxa, so in those studies a taxon missing from a signature may simply not have been measured (see "Assay coverage" above).

## Metadata captured by each database

```{r bsdb-fields}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Share of signatures with each field filled in, by database. BugSigDB records statistical methods and diversity; PerioSigDB records participant and clinical characteristics. Case group: periodontitis in PerioSigDB, the condition in BugSigDB; control group: health in PerioSigDB. 16S variable region: share of 16S signatures only (not applicable to other methods). –: field not in the database."

filled <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) return(lengths(x) > 0)
  !is.na(x) & !(as.character(x) %in% c("", "NA"))
}
field_share <- function(d, db, fields) {
  tibble(
    db = db, field = fields,
    share = map_dbl(fields, \(f) {
      if (!f %in% names(d)) return(NA_real_)
      # variable region applies to 16S signatures only
      keep <- if (f == "16S variable region") d$`Sequencing type` %in% c("16S", "16S,PCR") else TRUE
      mean(filled(d[[f]][keep]))
    })
  )
}

shared_fields <- c("Group 1 definition", "Group 0 sample size", "Group 1 sample size",
                   "Sequencing type", "16S variable region", "Sequencing platform", "Location of subjects")
bsdb_fields <- c("Statistical test", "Significance threshold", "MHT correction", "LDA Score above",
                 "Matched on", "Confounders controlled for", "Antibiotics exclusion", "Shannon", "Richness")
perio_fields <- c("Group 0 definition", "Periodontitis classification", "Systemic condition",
                  "Group 1 age mean", "Group 1 percent males", "Group 1 percent smokers",
                  "Group 1 pocket depth mean (mm)", "Group 1 clinical attachment loss (mm)",
                  "Group 1 bleeding on probing percent", "Group 1 plaque")
all_fields <- c(shared_fields, bsdb_fields, perio_fields)
# fields shared with BugSigDB name the case and control groups; PerioSigDB-only fields are periodontitis and health
field_label <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x %in% shared_fields,
         sub("^Group 0 (.)", "Control group \\L\\1", sub("^Group 1 (.)", "Case group \\L\\1", x, perl = TRUE), perl = TRUE),
         sub("^Group 0 ", "Health ", sub("^Group 1 ", "Periodontitis ", x)))
}

fields_db <- bind_rows(
  field_share(dat, "PerioSigDB", all_fields),
  field_share(bsdb_other, "BugSigDB", all_fields)
) |>
  mutate(
    # classification "not specified" counts as missing
    share = ifelse(db == "PerioSigDB" & field == "Periodontitis classification",
                   mean(dat$`Periodontitis classification` != "Periodontitis (type not specified)"), share),
    field_type = case_when(
      field %in% shared_fields ~ "Both databases",
      field %in% bsdb_fields ~ "BugSigDB only",
      .default = "PerioSigDB only"
    ),
    field = factor(field_label(field), levels = rev(field_label(all_fields))),
    db = factor(db, levels = db_levels)
  )

ggplot(fields_db, aes(x = db, y = field)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = share, fill = db), shape = 21, color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(share), "–", scales::percent(share, 1))),
            nudge_x = 0.22, hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(field_type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_db, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.7))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** share of signatures (PerioSigDB 201; BugSigDB 8,114, periodontitis excluded) with the field filled; area ∝ share, % printed beside it. "–" = column absent from that database.
- **Filled:** not NA, not "" and not the text "NA"; list fields filled if non-empty. "ND" counts as filled. PerioSigDB classification counts as missing when "type not specified" (63.7% filled).
- **Unit:** signatures, so PerioSigDB studies with two signatures count twice (shares differ slightly from the study-level completeness heatmap, e.g. age 85.6% here vs 83% both groups there).
- **Rows:** "Both databases" fields use BugSigDB names (Group 1 → case group, Group 0 → control group). "PerioSigDB only" clinical fields are Group 1 (periodontitis) values only; Group 0 definition shows as "Health definition".
- **16S variable region:** denominator is 16S signatures only (`Sequencing type` 16S or 16S,PCR): 66 in PerioSigDB (51.5% filled), 6,715 in BugSigDB (92.7%).
- **Plaque here:** any non-missing `Group 1 plaque` (indices included), unlike the heatmap, which counts % sites only.
- **Example:** sequencing type is filled for 63.2% of PerioSigDB vs 99.1% of BugSigDB signatures; the 50 hybridization signatures account for most of the PerioSigDB gap. BugSigDB `Shannon` (61.7%) counts "unchanged" entries as filled.
- **No test.**
:::

**Shows:** the two databases record complementary metadata. PerioSigDB adds participant and clinical characteristics for which BugSigDB does not currently include dedicated fields. BugSigDB records the statistical test, significance threshold, multiple-testing correction and matching, which PerioSigDB lacks. Adding those fields would improve the metadata compatibility of PerioSigDB with BugSigDB; a full import would also need validation against BugSigDB's schema and vocabularies.

**Caveats:**

- A filled field is not necessarily a complete one (e.g. "Matched on" can list only some of the variables).
- PerioSigDB's lower sequencing type completeness is mostly checkerboard hybridization, which has no sequencing type in BugSigDB's vocabulary.

## PerioSigDB taxa across other conditions

```{r bsdb-conditions-data}
# genera with the most consistent direction in PerioSigDB: exact binomial test of increased vs
# decreased signatures against 50% (as for taxa in the main report), then how often the top 20
# in each direction appear in BugSigDB signatures of the same direction for each other condition
n_sig_dir <- table(dat$`Abundance in Group 1`)

perio_tests <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    signatures = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased")
  )

perio_genera <- perio_tests |>
  filter(!is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(p, desc(signatures)) |>
  slice_head(n = 20, by = direction) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05",
      p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05 (not FDR)",
      .default = "Not significant"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)", "Not significant"))
  )

# participants (both groups) of the PerioSigDB studies reporting each genus in its periodontitis
# direction, each study counted once
perio_participants <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  mutate(Study = dat$Study[sig]) |>
  distinct(Study, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(transmute(studies, Study, n = `Group 0 sample size` + `Group 1 sample size`), by = "Study") |>
  summarise(participants = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(taxon, direction))
perio_genera <- left_join(perio_genera, perio_participants, by = c("taxon", "direction"))

# body site group of each signature (signatures listing sites in several groups are "mixed")
site_group <- function(sites) {
  map_chr(strsplit(sites, ","), function(x) {
    groups <- unique(site_of(x))
    if (length(groups) == 1) groups else "mixed"
  })
}

# disease (or exposure) vs control comparisons only: Group 0 is a control group and Group 1 is not.
# This drops body site, time point, treatment arm, diet and reversed comparisons, which BugSigDB
# also files under the study's condition
control_names <- paste0("control|healthy|\\bhealth\\b|normal|\\bnon[- ]?|without|negative|unaffected|",
                        "\\bHC\\b|\\bNC\\b|cognitively (intact|unimpaired)|^no\\b|-free\\b|peritumo|adjacent|benign")
# BugSigDB condition labels that name the same condition (different ontology terms), merged
condition_synonyms <- c(
  "Colorectal carcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer", "Colorectal adenocarcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer",
  "Colon carcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer",
  "Major depressive disorder" = "Unipolar depression",
  "Human immunodeficiency virus" = "HIV infection",
  "Eczema" = "Atopic eczema",
  "Autism" = "Autism spectrum disorder",
  "Breast carcinoma" = "Breast cancer",
  "Esophageal carcinoma" = "Esophageal cancer",
  "Human papillomavirus" = "Human papilloma virus infection",
  "Gastric adenocarcinoma" = "Gastric cancer",
  "Prostate carcinoma" = "Prostate cancer",
  "Psoriasis vulgaris" = "Psoriasis",
  "Autoimmune type 1 diabetes" = "Type I diabetes mellitus",
  "SARS-CoV-2-related disease" = "COVID-19",
  "Constipation" = "Chronic constipation",
  # all oral, pharyngeal or laryngeal cancers
  "Squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer", "Oral squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer",
  "Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer", "Oral cavity carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer",
  "Head and neck carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer"
)

# human disease-vs-control comparisons only (PerioSigDB is human), excluding meta-analyses, which
# re-analyse cohorts that are also in BugSigDB as primary studies
bsdb_cc <- bsdb_other |>
  filter(`Host species` == "Homo sapiens",
         !grepl("meta-analysis", `Study design`),
         grepl(control_names, `Group 0 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !grepl(control_names, `Group 1 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         `Abundance in Group 1` %in% c("increased", "decreased")) |>
  mutate(Condition = coalesce(condition_synonyms[Condition], Condition))

# count each study once per condition, direction and body site group: the units below are
# study-level, and a genus is in a unit if it is in any of the study's signatures in that unit
bsdb_cc_sigs <- tibble(
  sig = seq_len(nrow(bsdb_cc)), bsdb_id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study,
  Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition, direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  oral = is_oral(bsdb_cc$`Body site`),
  site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`)
) |>
  mutate(unit = as.integer(factor(paste(Study, Condition, direction, site_group, sep = "|"))))

bsdb_sigs <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  summarise(oral = any(oral), .by = c(unit, Study, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  rename(sig = unit)

bsdb_genera <- sig_genera(bsdb_cc) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_cc_sigs, sig, unit), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(sig = unit, direction, taxon)

# direction of the periodontitis genera in each condition (genera reported by >= 3 of its studies)
genus_agreement <- bsdb_genera |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon) |>
  distinct(sig, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
  count(Condition, taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio = direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(n = increased + decreased, same = ifelse(perio == "increased", increased, decreased)) |>
  filter(n >= 3)

agreement_map <- genus_agreement |>
  # each genus counts once: mean over genera of the share of its reports in the same direction
  summarise(genera = n(), agree = sum(same / n > 0.5), share = mean(same / n), .by = c(Condition, perio)) |>
  filter(genera >= 3) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = perio, values_from = c(genera, agree, share)) |>
  filter(!is.na(share_increased), !is.na(share_decreased)) |>
  mutate(genera = genera_increased + genera_decreased, agree = agree_increased + agree_decreased,
         label = Condition,
         p = map2_dbl(agree, genera, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n)$p.value))


# left panel: PerioSigDB signatures with the genus increased (right) and decreased (left), and
# participants in the studies reporting it in its periodontitis direction (circles)
perio_panel <- function(top, genus_levels) {
  perio_counts <- top |>
    select(taxon, increased, decreased, significance) |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))

  max_n <- max(abs(perio_counts$n))
  ggplot(perio_counts, aes(x = n, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels))) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = significance), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = distinct(top, taxon, fdr),
              aes(x = -max_n * 1.05, label = ifelse(fdr < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", fdr))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.5, color = "grey30") +
    geom_point(data = distinct(top, taxon, participants), aes(x = max_n * 1.35, size = participants),
               shape = 21, fill = "grey65", color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 6.5, limits = c(0, max(perio_genera$participants)), breaks = c(500, 2000, 5000),
                    name = "Participants") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = NULL) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                       drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = scales::breaks_extended()(c(-max_n, max_n)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.25))) +
    labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures\n(left: FDR; circles: participants)", y = NULL) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 1), alpha = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1),
           size = guide_legend(order = 3, ncol = 1)) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}

# top bar: share of each column's signatures from oral body sites
oral_panel <- function(columns) {
  ggplot(columns, aes(x = col, y = oral)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey60", width = 0.7) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Oral sites") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
}

# one-sided test of a genus being in a condition's signatures more often than in other conditions'
# signatures from the same body site group; strata without both are uninformative and dropped
site_matched_p <- function(condition, genus, sigs, hits) {
  d <- sigs |>
    mutate(in_condition = Condition == condition, has_genus = sig %in% hits$sig[hits$taxon == genus])
  informative <- d |>
    summarise(ok = any(in_condition) & any(!in_condition), .by = site_group) |>
    filter(ok) |>
    pull(site_group)
  if (!length(informative)) return(NA_real_)
  d <- filter(d, site_group %in% informative)
  tab <- table(factor(d$in_condition, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$has_genus, c(TRUE, FALSE)),
               factor(d$site_group))
  if (dim(tab)[3] == 1) {
    fisher.test(tab[, , 1], alternative = "greater")$p.value
  } else {
    mantelhaen.test(tab, exact = TRUE, alternative = "greater")$p.value
  }
}

# observed and expected share of a condition's signatures with each genus, where expected is the
# share in other conditions' signatures from the same body site group, weighted by the condition's
# own site mix; only site groups with signatures from both are used (as in site_matched_p)
site_expected <- function(sigs, hits) {
  by_group <- count(sigs, Condition, site_group, name = "n")
  hits_by_group <- hits |>
    left_join(select(sigs, sig, Condition, site_group), by = "sig") |>
    count(Condition, site_group, taxon, name = "h")
  totals <- count(sigs, site_group, name = "N")
  hit_totals <- count(hits_by_group, site_group, taxon, wt = h, name = "H")

  tidyr::expand_grid(by_group, taxon = unique(hits$taxon)) |>
    left_join(hits_by_group, by = c("Condition", "site_group", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(totals, by = "site_group") |>
    left_join(hit_totals, by = c("site_group", "taxon")) |>
    mutate(h = coalesce(h, 0L), H = coalesce(H, 0L)) |>
    filter(N > n) |>
    summarise(observed = sum(h) / sum(n), expected = sum(n * (H - h) / (N - n)) / sum(n),
              .by = c(Condition, taxon))
}

# match_site = TRUE compares each condition with other signatures from the same body site group
# (exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by site group) instead of all other signatures
# enrichment of each genus in each condition's signatures, vs all other BugSigDB signatures of this
# direction (one-sided Fisher's exact test) or vs other signatures from the same body site group
# (match_site), BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests; cached as it is used twice
enrichment_cache <- new.env()
enrichment_table <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, match_site = FALSE) {
  key <- paste(dir, min_sigs, match_site)
  if (!is.null(enrichment_cache[[key]])) return(enrichment_cache[[key]])
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(direction == dir, taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon)
  condition_sizes <- sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)
  genus_totals <- count(hits, taxon, name = "with_genus")
  enrichment_cache[[key]] <- hits |>
    left_join(select(sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
    count(Condition, taxon, name = "n") |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = condition_sizes$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    mutate(
      n = coalesce(n, 0L), with_genus = coalesce(with_genus, 0L),
      share = n / signatures,
      p = if (match_site) {
        map2_dbl(Condition, taxon, site_matched_p, sigs = sigs, hits = hits)
      } else {
        pmap_dbl(list(n, signatures, with_genus), function(a, n_cond, n_genus) {
          fisher.test(matrix(c(a, n_cond - a, n_genus - a, nrow(sigs) - n_cond - n_genus + a), 2),
                      alternative = "greater")$p.value
        })
      },
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )
  enrichment_cache[[key]]
}

condition_heatmap <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, match_site = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(direction == dir, taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon)
  genus_totals <- count(hits, taxon, name = "with_genus")
  enrichment <- enrichment_table(dir, min_sigs, match_site)

  # conditions of the shared set, ordered by most significantly enriched genera (ties: combined p-value)
  conditions <- enrichment |>
    filter(Condition %in% figure_conditions(enrichment)) |>
    summarise(n_enriched = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), score = sum(-log10(p), na.rm = TRUE),
              .by = c(Condition, signatures, oral)) |>
    arrange(desc(n_enriched), desc(score))

  # first column: all BugSigDB signatures of this direction (baseline)
  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(sigs), oral = mean(sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"), col = factor(col, levels = col))

  baseline <- tibble(taxon = top$taxon) |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    transmute(Condition = "All BugSigDB", taxon, share = coalesce(with_genus, 0L) / nrow(sigs), fdr = NA_real_)

  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)
  high <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"

  if (match_site) {
    # site-matched: colour and label are observed / expected (no unmatched baseline column)
    columns <- filter(columns, Condition != "All BugSigDB") |> mutate(col = droplevels(col))
    shares <- filter(enrichment, Condition %in% conditions$Condition) |>
      select(Condition, taxon, n, fdr) |>
      left_join(site_expected(sigs, hits), by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
      left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
      mutate(
        enriched = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
        # ratios from a single study are unstable, so only cells with at least 2 studies are shaded
        ratio = ifelse(coalesce(expected, 0) > 0 & n >= 2, observed / expected, NA),
        value = ifelse(is.na(ratio), 0, log2(pmax(ratio, 1))),
        label = ifelse(!is.na(ratio) & (enriched | ratio >= 2),
                       ifelse(ratio < 10, sprintf("%.1f", ratio), sprintf("%.0f", ratio)), "")
      )
    fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = high, limits = c(0, 4), oob = scales::squish,
                                      breaks = 0:4, labels = paste0("×", 2^(0:4)), na.value = "white",
                                      name = "Observed /\nexpected")
    dark <- quote(value > 2.5)
  } else {
    shares <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(enrichment, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
      select(Condition, taxon, share, fdr) |>
      left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
      mutate(enriched = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05, value = share,
             label = ifelse(enriched | share >= 0.1, round(100 * share), ""))
    fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = high, labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA),
                                      name = "BugSigDB\nstudies")
    dark <- quote(value > 0.45)
  }

  p_heat <- ggplot(shares, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = value)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(shares, enriched), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    (if (!match_site) geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, color = !!dark, fontface = ifelse(enriched, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.7) +
    fill_scale +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey20", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it increased vs decreased against 50% (the same test as for PerioSigDB),
# BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it in the same vs the opposite direction as periodontitis
count_directions <- function(d, ...) {
  d |>
    count(..., taxon, direction) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                  decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))()
}
direction_test <- function(d, dir) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      n = increased + decreased,
      same = if (dir == "increased") increased else decreased,
      share_same = same / n,
      p = map2_dbl(same, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )
}
direction_hits <- function(dir) {
  bsdb_genera |>
    filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon[perio_genera$direction == dir]) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon) |>
    left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, direction), by = "sig") |>
    filter(direction %in% c("increased", "decreased"))
}
direction_tests <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5) {
  sizes <- bsdb_sigs |> count(Condition, name = "signatures") |> filter(signatures >= min_sigs)
  direction_hits(dir) |>
    filter(Condition %in% sizes$Condition) |>
    count_directions(Condition) |>
    direction_test(dir)
}

direction_heatmap <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)
  hits <- direction_hits(dir)
  condition_sizes <- bsdb_sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)
  tests <- direction_tests(dir, min_sigs)

  baseline <- hits |>
    count_directions() |>
    direction_test(dir) |>
    mutate(Condition = "All BugSigDB")

  # conditions of the shared set, ordered by the mean over genera reported by at least min_reports
  # studies of the share of each genus's reports in the same direction as periodontitis
  conditions <- tests |>
    filter(n >= min_reports, Condition %in% figure_conditions(tests)) |>
    summarise(share = mean(same / n), .by = Condition) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    arrange(desc(share))

  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(bsdb_sigs), oral = mean(bsdb_sigs$oral), share = NA),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral, share)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = ifelse(is.na(share), paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"),
                        sprintf("%s (%d; %.0f%%)", Condition, signatures, 100 * share)),
           col = factor(col, levels = col))

  cells <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(tests, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = columns$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(
      significant = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
      # too few signatures to show a direction
      few = !is.na(n) & n < 3,
      share_plot = ifelse(few, NA, share_same),
      label = ifelse(!is.na(n) & !few, paste0(same, "/", n), "")
    )

  same_col <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"
  opposite_col <- if (dir == "increased") "#1c5cab" else "#c2410c"

  p_heat <- ggplot(cells, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = share_plot)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, few), fill = "grey85", color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, significant), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(significant, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.4, color = "grey15") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = opposite_col, mid = "#f0efec", high = same_col, midpoint = 0.5,
                         limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent, na.value = "white",
                         name = paste0("Studies\nreporting it\n", dir)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# whole-signature similarity (see "Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis")
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R (takes ~20 minutes)
semsim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")
# Lin similarity of each BugSigDB taxon to the consensus taxa, with taxon lineages
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.R
taxon_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.rds")

# similarity ranks among BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (and body site group if match_site)
similarity_ranks <- function(match_site = TRUE) {
  units <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
    # signatures with at least 5 taxa (as in the BugSigDB paper): smaller ones give extreme, noisy similarities
    filter(lengths(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig]) >= 5) |>
    inner_join(semsim$similarity, by = c("bsdb_id" = "BSDB ID")) |>
    summarise(up = mean(sim_increased), down = mean(sim_decreased),
              .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
    mutate(up = (rank(up) - 0.5) / n(), down = (rank(down) - 0.5) / n(),
           .by = all_of(if (match_site) c("direction", "site_group") else "direction")) |>
    filter(n() >= 5, .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
    pivot_longer(c(up, down), names_to = "perio", values_to = "rank") |>
    mutate(perio = ifelse(perio == "up", "increased", "decreased"))

  # one-sided: more similar than typical, within each BugSigDB direction x periodontitis signature
  stats <- units |>
    summarise(
      studies = n(),
      mean_rank = mean(rank),
      ci = 1.96 * sd(rank) / sqrt(n()),
      p = wilcox.test(rank, mu = 0.5, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)$p.value,
      .by = c(Condition, direction, perio)
    ) |>
    mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(direction, perio))

  list(units = units, stats = stats)
}

semsim_site <- similarity_ranks()
semsim_all <- similarity_ranks(match_site = FALSE)

# conditions shown: those with enough data in both directions (at least 3 periodontitis genera
# reported by at least 3 studies in each) in every figure, plus, in each figure, any condition with
# p < 0.05 in that figure's own tests; each figure orders them by its own criterion
base_conditions <- agreement_map$Condition
figure_conditions <- function(tests) union(base_conditions, tests$Condition[!is.na(tests$p) & tests$p < 0.05])
```

In which other conditions does the microbiome literature (BugSigDB) report the taxa that PerioSigDB links to periodontitis? BugSigDB is restricted to human disease-vs-control comparisons, excluding meta-analyses (`r nrow(bsdb_cc)` signatures from `r n_distinct(bsdb_cc$Study)` studies), and each study counts once per condition, direction and body site group. Body site groups: oral (mouth, saliva, dental plaque, tongue, gums, inner cheek, lip), upper airway (throat, pharynx including the oropharynx, nose), lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye and other (e.g. blood, milk); signatures listing sites from several groups are mixed. Condition labels that name the same condition are merged (e.g. colorectal carcinoma into colorectal cancer; oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal cancers into head and neck cancer).

Every figure below shows the same `r length(base_conditions)` core conditions, those with at least 3 periodontitis genera reported by at least 3 studies in each direction, plus any other condition with unadjusted p < 0.05 in that figure's own tests.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to read the genus heatmaps

- **Rows:** the top 20 periodontitis-increased or -decreased genera (see the taxon set table above), most significant at top. Not all of them pass FDR in PerioSigDB.
- **Left panel:** PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus decreased (bars to the left) or increased (bars to the right), with the FDR of a binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50%. Bar shading: FDR < 0.05, unadjusted p < 0.05, or neither. Circles: total participants (periodontitis and comparison groups) in the PerioSigDB studies reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction, each study counted once; this shows how many participants support each genus, which the number of signatures does not.
- **Columns:** BugSigDB conditions; in brackets, the number of the condition's studies (study units) of the direction shown, i.e. studies with any signature of that direction, not only those reporting the displayed genera.
- **Top bar:** share of the condition's studies from oral sites.
- **Outlined cells with bold numbers:** FDR < 0.05 for the test named in each caption, adjusted across all genera and all conditions tested, including conditions not shown. The All BugSigDB column is not tested in the enrichment heatmaps; in the direction heatmaps it is adjusted separately, across its 20 genera.
- **Empty cells:** not reported, or too few studies to show a value (each caption gives the minimum). A study reporting a genus in both directions (e.g. different species of it, or different comparisons) counts once in each direction.
:::

### Periodontitis-associated genera reported more often in other conditions

*Is the genus reported more often in this condition than in others?*

```{r bsdb-conditions-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-increased genera and how often other conditions report them increased (BugSigDB). Columns: all of BugSigDB, then each condition, ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus increased (numbers, in %, shown when at least 10% or enriched); empty: not reported. Outlined: one-sided Fisher's exact test of the share of the condition's studies with the genus vs the share of all other BugSigDB studies of this direction."
condition_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-conditions-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-decreased genera and how often other conditions report them decreased (BugSigDB). Columns: all of BugSigDB, then each condition, ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus decreased (numbers, in %, shown when at least 10% or enriched); empty: not reported. Outlined: one-sided Fisher's exact test of the share of the condition's studies with the genus vs the share of all other BugSigDB studies of this direction."
condition_heatmap("decreased")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Question:** is the genus listed in this condition's signatures of the same direction more often than in the rest of BugSigDB? It tests how often the genus is reported, not its direction. A condition reporting it in the opposite direction is not counted here (see the direction figures).
- **PerioSigDB rows:** each PerioSigDB taxon is reduced to its MetaPhlAn `g__` genus; taxa above genus rank are dropped, and a genus counts once per signature. For each of the 192 genera, an exact binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50% is run, BH-adjusted across all 192 (the FDR in the left panel). Genera with equal counts in both directions have no direction and are left out. The top 20 per direction are ranked by p, with ties broken by more signatures. Rows 14–20 (from *Campylobacter* down) of the increased set and rows 6–20 (from *Neisseria* down) of the decreased set have FDR ≥ 0.05.
- **Left panel:** bar lengths are PerioSigDB signatures, not studies (201 signatures from 128 studies; one study can contribute several). For example, *Porphyromonas* has 82 increased and 10 decreased, FDR 2e-13.
- **Participant circles:** total Group 0 + Group 1 size of each PerioSigDB study reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction, each study counted once. The circle area is proportional to this total, on one scale shared by all genus figures (largest: *Porphyromonas* increased, 7,952). Three of 128 studies lack sample sizes and count as 0.
- **BugSigDB data:** non-periodontitis BugSigDB signatures from human studies, excluding meta-analyses and keeping only increased or decreased signatures. A signature is kept only if its Group 0 name matches a control pattern (control, healthy, normal, non-, without, negative, HC, adjacent, benign, …) and its Group 1 name does not. This keeps 3,208 of 6,218 signatures from 867 studies. Synonymous condition labels are merged (e.g. colorectal carcinoma, colorectal adenocarcinoma and colon carcinoma become colorectal cancer; oral, oral squamous cell and head and neck carcinomas become head and neck cancer).
- **Study unit:** one BugSigDB study × condition × direction × body site group, giving 1,892 units: 974 increased and 918 decreased. A genus is in a unit if any of the unit's signatures lists it at genus or species rank. Units whose signatures list no genus still count in the denominators.
- **Each cell:** the share of the condition's units of this direction that contain the genus. For example, *Fusobacterium* in colorectal cancer is 54% = 29 of 54 increased colorectal cancer units.
- **All BugSigDB column:** units of this direction from all conditions, including small ones and the condition itself; for example, *Fusobacterium* is in 125 of 974 (13%). This column is not tested.
- **Brackets and top bar:** the number of the condition's units of this direction. The top bar is the share of those units with any oral body site (e.g. colorectal cancer 9%, smoking 88%, increased).
- **Conditions tested:** the 40 conditions with ≥ 5 units of the direction. Shown are 11 core conditions plus any with unadjusted p < 0.05: 16 columns for increased (adds HPV infection, response to transplant, cervical glandular intraepithelial neoplasia, diarrhoea, multiple sclerosis) and 16 for decreased (adds dry eye syndrome, atopic eczema, chronic kidney disease, response to immunochemotherapy, chronic fatigue syndrome).
- **Test:** a one-sided Fisher's exact test on a 2×2 table: the condition's units with and without the genus vs all other units of this direction with and without it. The BH correction covers all 800 genus × condition tests per direction, including conditions not shown.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer × *Fusobacterium* is 29 of 54 (54%) vs 96 of 920 other increased units (10%), OR 9.9, p = 8e-14, FDR = 2e-11. Rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema* is 5 of 13 vs 27 of 961 (3%), FDR = 0.005. Head and neck cancer × *Rothia* (decreased) is 7 of 15 vs 49 of 903 (5%), FDR = 0.004.
- **All FDR < 0.05 cells:** for increased, colorectal cancer × *Peptostreptococcus*, *Parvimonas*, *Fusobacterium* and *Porphyromonas*, plus rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema*. For decreased, head and neck cancer × *Rothia* and *Actinomyces*, smoking × *Gemella*, *Capnocytophaga* and *Lautropia*, and COVID-19 × *Neisseria*.
- **Watch out:** there is no adjustment for body site (oral genera are enriched in any oral condition; see the next figure) or for signature length (long signatures include more genera by chance). Small conditions with 5–15 units give large shares from few studies.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer studies disproportionately report increases in *Porphyromonas*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Fusobacterium*. Oral conditions also appear enriched: rheumatoid arthritis for increases in *Treponema*, and, among the periodontitis-decreased genera, head and neck cancer (*Actinomyces*, *Rothia*), smoking (*Capnocytophaga*, *Gemella*, *Lautropia*) and COVID-19 (*Neisseria*). These oral genera are common in any oral sample, so the next section compares conditions within body site groups.

### Enrichment compared within body site groups

Here each condition is compared only with studies from the same broad body site groups. "Oral" is broad: it includes saliva, tongue and other oral sites as well as plaque.

```{r bsdb-site-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-increased genera and how often other conditions report them increased (BugSigDB), compared within body site groups. Columns ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus increased divided by the share expected from other conditions' studies from the same body site groups, weighted by the condition's own site mix. Shaded only with at least 2 studies reporting the genus; empty: not reported, 1 study, or no expected value. Numbers shown when ×2 or more or enriched; large ratios from 2–3 studies are uncertain unless outlined. Outlined: one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test of the condition's studies with the genus vs other conditions' studies, stratified by body site group (oral, upper airway, lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye, other, mixed)."
condition_heatmap("increased", match_site = TRUE)
```

```{r bsdb-site-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-decreased genera and how often other conditions report them decreased (BugSigDB), compared within body site groups. Columns ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus decreased divided by the share expected from other conditions' studies from the same body site groups, weighted by the condition's own site mix. Shaded only with at least 2 studies reporting the genus; empty: not reported, 1 study, or no expected value. Numbers shown when ×2 or more or enriched; large ratios from 2–3 studies are uncertain unless outlined. Outlined: one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test of the condition's studies with the genus vs other conditions' studies, stratified by body site group (oral, upper airway, lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye, other, mixed)."
condition_heatmap("decreased", match_site = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Data:** the same as the previous figure: the same units, genera and 40 tested conditions. The only change is that each condition is compared with other conditions' units from the same body site group. There is no All BugSigDB column.
- **Body site group:** each unit has one group (oral, upper airway, lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye, other), or "mixed" if its signatures' sites span several groups. Of all 1,892 units, 1,249 are gastrointestinal and 260 oral. The top bar still shows the share of units with any oral site.
- **Each cell (observed / expected):** observed is the condition's share of units with the genus. Expected averages, over the condition's site groups and weighted by its number of units in each, the share of other conditions' units in that group with the genus. Groups where the condition is the only one are skipped.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer × *Fusobacterium* is observed 54% (29/54) vs expected 8.6% (gastrointestinal: 28 of 48 colorectal cancer units vs 42 of 583 other units; oral: 1 of 5 vs 28 of 133), giving ×6.3. Other colorectal cancer ratios: *Parvimonas* ×13, *Peptostreptococcus* ×12, *Porphyromonas* ×6.6.
- **Shading rules:** a cell is shaded only if ≥ 2 of the condition's units have the genus (e.g. colorectal cancer × *Pseudoramibacter*, 1 unit at ×2.8, is blank). The colour is log2(ratio) capped at ×16. Ratios below 1 get the palest colour, so depletion is not shown. Numbers appear when ×2 or more, or when outlined.
- **Test:** a one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test (`mantelhaen.test(exact = TRUE)`). It uses 2×2 tables (condition vs other × genus present vs absent) stratified by site group and tests a common odds ratio > 1. Strata without units from both the condition and others are dropped; with a single informative stratum, it is a one-sided Fisher's test. BH covers all 800 genus × condition tests per direction.
- **Result:** only colorectal cancer × *Peptostreptococcus*, *Parvimonas*, *Fusobacterium* and *Porphyromonas* have FDR < 0.05 (e.g. *Fusobacterium* p = 3e-15, FDR = 8e-13). No decreased cell passes.
- **What changed:** rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema* is ×4.2 (5 of 8 oral rheumatoid arthritis units vs 19 of 130 other oral units), p = 0.005, FDR = 0.39. Smoking × *Gemella* is ×5.0, p = 0.001, FDR = 0.53. Head and neck cancer × *Rothia* is ×2.3, p = 0.02, FDR = 1. COVID-19 × *Neisseria* is ×2.7, p = 0.01, FDR = 1. These ratios stay high but are no longer significant once compared with other oral (or upper airway) studies.
- **Conditions shown:** the 11 core conditions plus any with p < 0.05 in this test. For increased, that adds response to transplant, treatment outcome measurement, diarrhoea and multiple sclerosis. For decreased, it adds atopic eczema, chronic fatigue syndrome, chronic kidney disease, psoriasis, response to immunochemotherapy, schizophrenia, type I diabetes and unipolar depression.
- **Watch out:** "oral" lumps plaque, saliva, tongue and mucosa, so plaque-specific genera can still look enriched in oral conditions sampled from plaque. Large ratios from 2–3 units are imprecise. The number of other units in a stratum can be small (e.g. 16–18 in eye or lower airway).
:::

**Shows:** after stratification by body site group, only colorectal cancer remains significant, with the same four genera. None of the oral-condition enrichments remained significant after BH correction, which suggests that shared sampling sites contribute substantially to the unstratified overlap.

### Direction of periodontitis-associated genera within each condition

*When the condition reports the genus, is it in the same direction as in periodontitis?*

```{r bsdb-direction-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-increased genera and the direction other conditions report them in (BugSigDB). Columns: all of BugSigDB, then each condition with, in brackets, its number of studies (both directions) and the mean over genera (reported by at least 3 of its studies) of the share of each genus's reports that are increased; ordered by that share, highest first. Cells: studies reporting the genus increased / all studies reporting it; colour: that share (orange: increased, as in periodontitis; blue: decreased). Grey: 1–2 studies; white: not reported. Outlined: two-sided binomial test of studies reporting the genus increased vs decreased against 50%, so an outlined cell can be significant in either direction."
direction_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-direction-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-decreased genera and the direction other conditions report them in (BugSigDB). Columns: all of BugSigDB, then each condition with, in brackets, its number of studies (both directions) and the mean over genera (reported by at least 3 of its studies) of the share of each genus's reports that are decreased; ordered by that share, highest first. Cells: studies reporting the genus decreased / all studies reporting it; colour: that share (blue: decreased, as in periodontitis; orange: increased). Grey: 1–2 studies; white: not reported. Outlined: two-sided binomial test of studies reporting the genus decreased vs increased against 50%, so an outlined cell can be significant in either direction."
direction_heatmap("decreased")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Question:** among the condition's units that report the genus in either direction, what share report it in the periodontitis direction? It ignores how often the genus is reported relative to other conditions (see the enrichment figures).
- **Each cell:** "same / n", where n is the condition's units reporting the genus increased plus units reporting it decreased. The colour is the share in the periodontitis direction. For example, colorectal cancer × *Fusobacterium* is 29/34 (29 increased, 5 decreased).
- **Counting:** units are the same as in the enrichment figures (study × condition × direction × body site group). A study listing the genus in both an increased and a decreased signature counts once in each. This happens for 87 study × condition × genus combinations among the periodontitis-increased genera.
- **Grey and white cells:** grey means 1–2 units, with no share or label shown. These cells are still tested and can never reach p < 0.05. White means not reported.
- **Brackets:** the condition's units of both directions (e.g. colorectal cancer 105). The % is the mean, over genera with n ≥ 3, of the share in the periodontitis direction; it orders the columns. The same per-condition values are the x (increased figure) and y (decreased figure) of the next figure.
- **Conditions:** tests cover the conditions with ≥ 5 units across both directions (67 for increased, 66 for decreased, since only conditions reporting at least one of the genera have tests). Only the 11 core conditions are shown, as no other condition has p < 0.05.
- **Test:** a two-sided exact binomial test of same vs opposite direction against 50%, BH-adjusted across all genus × condition tests per figure (432 increased, 464 decreased), including conditions not shown.
- **All BugSigDB column:** pools all 1,892 units from every condition, including small ones. It has its own BH correction across its 20 genera, so its outlines are not part of the condition family. Increased genera: *Fusobacterium* 125/189 (FDR 7e-5), *Parvimonas* 64/82, *Peptostreptococcus* 71/92, *Porphyromonas* 91/149 and *Selenomonas* 45/67 lean increased. Decreased genera: *Haemophilus* 130/204 lean decreased (FDR 0.001), while *Streptococcus* 144/384, *Actinomyces* 58/158 and *Gemella* 40/108 lean increased, the opposite of periodontitis.
- **Significant condition cells:** only colorectal cancer: *Peptostreptococcus* 25/25 (FDR 3e-5), *Parvimonas* 22/22 (1e-4), *Porphyromonas* 20/21 (0.003) and *Fusobacterium* 29/34 (0.004), all in the periodontitis direction. *Gemella* is 0/15 decreased, i.e. 15 of 15 increased (FDR 0.03), the opposite direction.
- **Example of a non-significant cell:** head and neck cancer × *Rothia* is 7/8 decreased (p = 0.07, FDR = 1). Small n per cell gives little power after correction across ~450 tests.
- **Watch out:** a share near 50% can mean genuinely mixed reports or very few reports, so read it together with n. The direction of a genus in a unit comes from genus or species entries, so different species of one genus can push opposite ways.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer is the only condition with genera whose direction differs significantly from 50% after BH correction: *Peptostreptococcus* (25/25 studies increased), *Parvimonas* (22/22), *Porphyromonas* (20/21) and *Fusobacterium* (29/34), all in the same direction as periodontitis. Its *Gemella*, decreased in periodontitis, is significant in the opposite direction (15/15 studies increased). The next figure summarises both directions for every condition.

#### Conditions with similar directions of association across periodontitis-associated genera

Each condition is summarised over all the periodontitis-associated genera its studies report, averaged over genera so that each genus counts once. This shows the direction of reports only: not how often the genera are reported compared with other conditions (see the enrichment heatmaps for that), and not whether the genera change together within participants.

```{r bsdb-agreement-map}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-cap: "Direction of the periodontitis-associated genera in each BugSigDB condition. x: mean over the periodontitis-increased genera of the share of each genus's reports in the condition that are increased; y: the same for the periodontitis-decreased genera and reports that are decreased. Genera counted are those among the 20 per direction in the genus heatmaps reported by at least 3 of the condition's studies; conditions shown have at least 3 such genera in each direction. Point size: number of genera counted. Shaded: same direction as periodontitis for both genus groups. Sign test (unadjusted p-values in the text): number of genera with more than half of their reports in the periodontitis direction against 50% of genera."
quadrants <- tibble(
  x = c(1, 1, 0, 0), y = c(1.06, -0.06, -0.06, 1.06), hjust = c(1, 1, 0, 0), vjust = c(1, 0, 0, 1),
  label = c("Same direction as periodontitis\nfor both genus groups", "Both genus groups\nreported increased",
            "Opposite to periodontitis\nfor both genus groups", "Both genus groups\nreported decreased")
)

ggplot(agreement_map, aes(share_increased, share_decreased)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 1, ymin = 0.5, ymax = 1, fill = "grey94") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_text(data = quadrants, aes(x, y, label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust), size = 3, color = "grey45",
            lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(size = genera), shape = 21, fill = "grey65", color = "grey15") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 3.1, color = "grey15", seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Genera counted") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(-0.06, 1.06), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Periodontitis-increased genera:\nshare of the condition's reports that are increased",
       y = "Periodontitis-decreased genera:\nshare of the condition's reports that are decreased") +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** one BugSigDB condition. Its x and y equal the bracketed % in the increased and decreased direction figures.
- **x:** over the periodontitis-increased genera (top 20) reported by ≥ 3 of the condition's units, the mean share of each genus's units reporting it increased. Each genus has equal weight, whatever its number of reports.
- **y:** the same over the periodontitis-decreased genera, using the share reported decreased.
- **Inclusion:** a condition needs ≥ 3 such genera in each direction. These 11 conditions are the core set shown in all heatmaps and similarity figures. There is no minimum on units beyond the ≥ 3 reports per genus.
- **Point size:** genera counted, both directions combined (e.g. COVID-19 26, colorectal cancer 17, Ulcerative colitis 6).
- **Sign test (not drawn; p-values in the text):** a two-sided exact binomial test of the number of genera with > 50% of reports in the periodontitis direction against 50% of genera counted. Genera at exactly 50% count as not agreeing (9 such genus × condition pairs). There is no correction across the 11 conditions.
- **Example (colorectal cancer):** x = 88% is the mean of *Campylobacter* 8/9, *Dialister* 9/12, *Fusobacterium* 29/34, *Mogibacterium* 5/6, *Parvimonas* 22/22, *Peptostreptococcus* 25/25, *Porphyromonas* 20/21, *Prevotella* 15/20 and *Selenomonas* 8/9. y = 33% is the mean of *Actinomyces* 5/11, *Corynebacterium* 1/6, *Gemella* 0/15, *Granulicatella* 0/4, *Haemophilus* 7/10, *Neisseria* 4/8, *Rothia* 2/5 and *Streptococcus* 10/24. That gives 10 of 17 genera agreeing (all 9 increased plus *Haemophilus*), sign test p = 0.63.
- **Other values:** head and neck cancer is x 66%, y 73%, 16 of 19 genera agreeing, p = 0.004. Smoking is 55% and 64%, 16 of 24, p = 0.15. COVID-19 is 37% and 51%, 7 of 26, p = 0.03. Ulcerative colitis has y = 0%, because its 3 periodontitis-decreased genera are always reported increased. Alzheimer's disease is 39% and 36%.
- **Watch out:** this shows direction only, not frequency or enrichment, and most shares rest on 3–10 units per genus. A condition can sit top right because a few genera agree weakly, so check the sign test and the direction heatmaps.
:::

```{r bsdb-agreement-values}
am <- \(cond, col) agreement_map[[col]][agreement_map$Condition == cond]
am_pct <- \(cond, col) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * am(cond, col))
```

**Shows:** three patterns. Sign tests across genera are unadjusted for the number of conditions.

- **Same direction as periodontitis for both genus groups (top right):** head and neck cancer (`r am("Head and neck cancer", "agree")` of `r am("Head and neck cancer", "genera")` genera agree, sign test p = `r signif(am("Head and neck cancer", "p"), 1)`) and, descriptively, smoking (`r am("Smoking behavior", "agree")` of `r am("Smoking behavior", "genera")`, p = `r signif(am("Smoking behavior", "p"), 1)`): the periodontitis-increased genera are mostly reported increased and the periodontitis-decreased genera decreased (*Haemophilus*, *Neisseria* and *Corynebacterium* decreased in both; also *Rothia* and *Actinomyces* in head and neck cancer, *Gemella* and *Lautropia* in smoking). Both are sampled mostly in the mouth, and smoking is a periodontitis risk factor.
- **Both genus groups reported increased (bottom right):** colorectal cancer, gastric cancer, ulcerative colitis and type 2 diabetes report the periodontitis-increased genera mostly increased (on average `r am_pct("Colorectal cancer", "share_increased")` of each genus's reports for colorectal cancer) and the periodontitis-decreased genera mostly increased too (`r am_pct("Colorectal cancer", "share_decreased")` decreased; e.g. *Gemella* in 15 of 15 colorectal cancer studies). The whole-signature similarity analyses below do not flag colorectal cancer's increased signatures as resembling the periodontitis-decreased signature, because they score whole signatures, in which these genera are a small part. For gastric cancer and ulcerative colitis they do. This pattern is compatible with increased representation of oral-associated genera in gastrointestinal disease, but does not establish their source or route of transfer.
- **Periodontitis-increased genera mostly reported decreased (left):** Alzheimer's disease lies in the quadrant opposite to periodontitis on both axes. COVID-19 (only `r am("COVID-19", "agree")` of `r am("COVID-19", "genera")` genera agree, p = `r signif(am("COVID-19", "p"), 1)`) and Parkinson's disease more often report the periodontitis-increased genera decreased, but their periodontitis-decreased genera are close to 50%, so they do not show a clear reversal of both genus groups.

### Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis

Compares whole signatures using taxa at their reported ranks (mostly species, with some genera and higher ranks), without collapsing to genus.

- **PerioSigDB consensus:** taxa more often increased (`r length(semsim$consensus$increased)`) or decreased (`r length(semsim$consensus$decreased)`) in periodontitis signatures (binomial test, unadjusted p < 0.05).
- **Similarity:** semantic similarity on the NCBI taxonomy (best-match average of Lin similarity, as in BugSigDB's tools), for BugSigDB signatures with at least 5 taxa (smaller ones give extreme scores).

```{r bsdb-semantic-c}

similarity_plot <- function(res, perio_dir, dir) {
  shown <- res$stats |>
    filter(perio == perio_dir, direction == dir) |>
    slice_min(p, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(label = paste0(Condition, " (", studies, ")\np = ", signif(p, 2), ", FDR = ", signif(fdr, 2)),
           label = fct_reorder(label, -p))
  points <- inner_join(res$units, select(shown, Condition, direction, perio, label),
                       by = c("Condition", "direction", "perio"))

  ggplot(shown, aes(y = label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_quasirandom(data = points, aes(x = rank), orientation = "y", width = 0.3, size = 1.1,
                     color = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6")[[perio_dir]], alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), height = 0, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey10") +
    geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = fdr < 0.05), shape = 21, size = 3.5, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey10", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Periodontitis %s vs BugSigDB %s", perio_dir, dir),
         subtitle = if (dir == perio_dir) "Same direction" else "Opposite direction",
         x = sprintf("Similarity to periodontitis-%s signature (rank; 0.5 = typical)", perio_dir), y = NULL) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey35"))
}

# one grid: conditions as rows (shared), the four comparisons as columns
comparison_levels <- c("Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB increased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB decreased",
                       "Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB decreased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB increased")

similarity_grid <- function(res, n_top = 5) {
  label_comparison <- function(d) {
    d |> mutate(
      comparison = factor(sprintf("Perio %s\nvs BugSigDB %s", perio, direction), levels = comparison_levels),
      opposite = perio != direction
    )
  }
  # union of the n_top conditions most similar to each periodontitis signature (same direction),
  # ordered by their smallest p in those two comparisons
  # conditions of the shared set, ordered by their smallest p in the same-direction comparisons
  conditions <- res$stats |>
    filter(Condition %in% figure_conditions(res$stats)) |>
    summarise(best = suppressWarnings(min(p[perio == direction])), .by = Condition) |>
    arrange(desc(best)) |>
    pull(Condition)

  stats <- res$stats |>
    filter(Condition %in% conditions) |>
    label_comparison() |>
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = conditions),
           significance = case_when(fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05", p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05", .default = "Not significant") |>
             factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05", "Not significant")))
  units <- res$units |>
    filter(Condition %in% conditions) |>
    label_comparison() |>
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = conditions))
  shade <- distinct(stats, comparison, opposite) |> filter(opposite)

  ggplot(stats, aes(y = Condition)) +
    geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "grey95") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_quasirandom(data = units, aes(x = rank, color = perio), orientation = "y", width = 0.3, size = 0.8,
                     alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), height = 0, linewidth = 0.7, color = "grey10") +
    geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = significance), shape = 21, size = 3, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = "grey10", "p < 0.05" = "grey60", "Not significant" = "white"),
                      name = "Mean", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    facet_grid(. ~ comparison) +
    labs(x = "Similarity (rank among BugSigDB study units; 0.5 = typical)", y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top",
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.8, "lines"))
}
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-all-fig}
#| fig-width: 13

#| fig-cap: "Similarity of BugSigDB signatures to the PerioSigDB consensus signatures. Each study unit's mean best-match average Lin similarity is ranked among BugSigDB study units of the same direction (0 = least, 1 = most similar; 0.5 = typical). Columns: similarity to the periodontitis-increased (orange points) or -decreased (blue points) consensus, for BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (white) or the opposite direction (shaded). Rows: conditions ordered by their smallest p-value in the two same-direction columns, most significant at top. Small points: study units; large point and bar: mean and 95% confidence interval. Large point black: FDR < 0.05; grey: unadjusted p < 0.05; one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the condition's ranks against 0.5 (BH within each column)."
similarity_grid(semsim_all)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **PerioSigDB consensus signatures:** taxa at their reported rank (species and genera are separate taxa; not collapsed). A taxon is in the consensus if it has more increased than decreased PerioSigDB signatures (or vice versa) with an exact binomial p < 0.05, unadjusted. This gives 33 increased and 13 decreased taxa. Precomputed by `scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R`.
- **Similarity of one BugSigDB signature:** Lin similarity on the NCBI taxonomy, based on how specific the taxa's most specific shared ancestor is. Information content is computed from descendant counts. The best-match average works in both directions: each consensus taxon is matched to its most similar taxon in the signature, those best scores are averaged, the same is done from the signature side, and the two averages are averaged (`ontologySimilarity::get_sim_grid`, `combine = "average"`). Partial credit therefore goes to relatives, e.g. a BugSigDB genus vs a PerioSigDB species of it.
- **Signatures used:** the same disease-vs-control signatures as the heatmaps, with ≥ 5 NCBI taxa (1,751 of 3,208). Taxa missing from the ontology are dropped. A unit's score is the mean over its signatures, giving 646 increased and 584 decreased units.
- **Rank:** (rank − 0.5) / N among all units of the same BugSigDB direction (all conditions, including small ones). Each unit is ranked separately for similarity to the increased consensus and to the decreased consensus. The ranks are used because raw scores vary little (median 0.42 among all increased units vs 0.48 for colorectal cancer).
- **Columns:** BugSigDB direction × consensus. The white columns pair same directions (the main test). The shaded columns pair opposite directions, e.g. "Perio decreased vs BugSigDB increased", which asks whether a condition's increased taxa resemble periodontitis-depleted (health-associated) taxa.
- **Test:** for each condition with ≥ 5 units of the BugSigDB direction (31 conditions per direction), a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of its units' ranks > 0.5 (normal approximation). BH runs within each column across those 31 conditions. The bar is the mean ± 1.96 SD/√n, a normal approximation and not a bootstrap.
- **Rows:** the 11 core conditions plus any with p < 0.05 in any column (here unipolar depression and dry eye syndrome), so 13 rows. A row has no point in a column if the condition has < 5 units of that direction.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer increased vs periodontitis-increased has 47 units with mean rank 0.71; 81% of units are above 0.5, p = 3e-5, FDR = 0.0008. Its other three columns have mean ranks of 0.46–0.48.
- **Next strongest (not FDR-significant):** head and neck cancer decreased vs decreased, 11 units, mean 0.84, p = 0.004, FDR = 0.14. Smoking decreased vs decreased, 12 units, 0.72, p = 0.01, FDR = 0.16. Head and neck cancer increased vs increased, 8 units, 0.76, p = 0.02.
- **Watch out:** ranks are relative to the rest of BugSigDB (mostly gut studies), so oral conditions look similar partly because they share oral taxa; the next figure corrects for this. The score covers the whole signature, so a few shared genera (e.g. colorectal cancer *Gemella*) barely move it.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer was the only condition meeting the FDR threshold: its increased taxa resemble the periodontitis-increased taxa (FDR = 0.0008). Several other conditions showed unadjusted evidence of similarity that did not remain significant after correction, so these are exploratory. Head and neck cancer showed the next strongest evidence: its decreased taxa resemble the periodontitis-decreased taxa (unadjusted p = 0.004, FDR = 0.14) and its increased taxa the periodontitis-increased ones (unadjusted p = 0.02). Smoking's decreased taxa resemble the periodontitis-decreased taxa (unadjusted p = 0.01). In the shaded column, the increased taxa of ulcerative colitis, gastric cancer and COVID-19 resemble the periodontitis-decreased taxa (unadjusted p ≈ 0.02), the "both genus groups reported increased" pattern of the direction summary above; gastric cancer resembles both periodontitis signatures.

#### Compared within body site groups

Here each study unit is ranked only among study units from the same body site group, so oral conditions are compared only with other oral ones.

Columns: similarity to the periodontitis-increased (orange points) or -decreased (blue points) consensus, for BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (white) or the opposite direction (shaded). Rows: conditions ordered by their smallest p-value in the two same-direction columns, most significant at top. Small points: study units; large point and bar: mean and 95% confidence interval. ```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Only change from the previous figure:** each unit is ranked among units of the same BugSigDB direction and body site group, so 0.5 means typical for that site. The similarity scores, consensus, units, test (one-sided Wilcoxon against 0.5, BH within each column over 31 conditions) and CI are the same.
- **Group sizes (units with ≥ 5 taxa, increased / decreased):** gastrointestinal 421 / 399, oral 93 / 87, urogenital 60 / 31, upper airway 24 / 22. Eye, lower airway, skin, other and mixed have 5–12 each, so ranks in those groups are coarse.
- **Rows:** the 11 core conditions plus any with p < 0.05 here (endometriosis, autism spectrum disorder, unipolar depression, schizophrenia), so 15 rows. The set and order differ from the previous figure.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer increased vs periodontitis-increased has 47 units, mean rank 0.72, p = 3e-5, FDR = 0.0008. It is nearly unchanged because 48 of its 54 increased units (with or without ≥ 5 taxa) are gastrointestinal and were mostly ranked against gut units already.
- **Oral conditions weaken:** head and neck cancer decreased goes from 0.84 to 0.63 (p = 0.05, FDR = 0.40). Smoking decreased goes from 0.72 to 0.53 (p = 0.39). Compared with other oral studies, their signatures are about average.
- **Shaded columns:** gastric cancer (0.70, p = 0.01) and ulcerative colitis (0.75, p = 0.02) increased vs periodontitis-decreased stay at unadjusted p < 0.05. Their increased taxa include health-associated oral genera even when compared with other gut studies.
- **Watch out:** none of the new rows (autism, schizophrenia, endometriosis, depression) passes FDR. Each has 6–10 units and many tests (31 per column × 4 columns), so expect some unadjusted hits by chance.
:::

```{r bsdb-semantic-site-values}
ss <- \(cond, dir) with(filter(semsim_site$stats, Condition == cond, direction == dir, perio == dir),
                        sprintf("p = %s, FDR = %s", signif(p, 1), signif(fdr, 1)))
```

**Shows:** colorectal cancer remains significant (`r ss("Colorectal cancer", "increased")`). Smoking no longer meets unadjusted p < 0.05 and head and neck cancer weakens (decreased taxa `r ss("Head and neck cancer", "decreased")`), as in the site-stratified enrichment: compared with other oral studies, their signatures are not unusually periodontitis-like. Gastric cancer's increased signatures still resemble both periodontitis signatures (unadjusted p < 0.05), consistent with oral taxa in general.

```{r bsdb-jaccard}
# the same tests with the BugSigDB paper's other measure: Jaccard overlap of genera
consensus_genera <- map(semsim$consensus, \(ids) {
  known <- unique(c(sig_genera(dat)$taxon, bsdb_genera$taxon))
  unique(na.omit(map_chr(strsplit(taxon_sim$lineage[ids], "|", fixed = TRUE), \(l) {
    hit <- which(l %in% known)
    if (length(hit)) l[max(hit)] else NA
  })))
})
jaccard <- \(a, b) length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
jaccard_units <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(lengths(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig]) >= 5) |>
  inner_join(summarise(sig_genera(bsdb_cc), g = list(unique(taxon)), .by = sig), by = "sig") |>
  mutate(up = map_dbl(g, jaccard, consensus_genera$increased), down = map_dbl(g, jaccard, consensus_genera$decreased)) |>
  summarise(up = mean(up), down = mean(down), .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group))
jaccard_tests <- map(c(all = FALSE, site = TRUE), \(match_site) {
  jaccard_units |>
    mutate(up = (rank(up) - 0.5) / n(), down = (rank(down) - 0.5) / n(),
           .by = all_of(if (match_site) c("direction", "site_group") else "direction")) |>
    filter(n() >= 5, .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
    pivot_longer(c(up, down), names_to = "perio", values_to = "rank") |>
    mutate(perio = ifelse(perio == "up", "increased", "decreased")) |>
    summarise(p = wilcox.test(rank, mu = 0.5, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)$p.value,
              .by = c(Condition, direction, perio)) |>
    mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(direction, perio))
})
```
